The DM will let you know which of these options to select

Default is that HP are tracked by the player for each level accumulated; HP are added to $Z$18. 
If this option is checked, then you can expand columns A through G on the ''Character Sheet'' and add HPs for each level and for each class. 
In either case the MAX HP will be displayed automatically on the ''Character Sheet'' in $X$21
If left blank Character sheet shows default Descending Armor Class (1e assumption and default OSRIC method). If checked shows Ascending (optional OSRIC method).
If DM tells you to use aging effects on ability scores check the check box to the left
if checked, the fighter, paladin, ranger, attack matrix progression is increased by 1 for every level (Also used in OSRIC 3.0). Default is to increase by 2 every 2 levels.
The default assumption for halflings (per PHB) is getting a +1 DEX bonus, and a max CON of 19.
This option makes the halfling ability adjustment and Maximum score consistent for Dexterity (Max DEX of 19, +1 bonus to DEX score)
This option makes the halfling ability adjustment and Maximum score consistent for Constitution (Max CON of 19, +1 bonus to CON score)

Default: Official Errata, Polyhedron issue #1 - Magic armor has no encumbrance (move at full movement rate, e.g. 120 for human).
OPTION: Magic armor encumbrance is 1 level better (per DMG 28), rather than having no encumbrance.
NOTE: for weight purposes magic armor is half the weight of non-magical armor (Will need to be done by user manually when entering weight of armor on the equipment list).
To Hit: Matrix vs Base To Hit Bonus (BTHB)

Default: uses the attack matrix from AD&D 1e.
If this box is checked use Base To Hit Bonus (BTHB) from optional OSRIC rule. Note this is slightly different than the attack matrix for magic attack bonus (e.g. from magic weapons), and can be used for ascending or descending Armor Class. Explanation:
1. For Ascending add this number to your attack d20 roll + any magic or situation bonuses to determine what AC you hit.
2. For Descending AC add this number to your attack d20 roll + any magic or situation bonuses and subtract oponents AC, if you score a 20 or above you hit.

For both, if you roll a natural 20 on the d20, add an additional +5 to your roll.

The default (box not checked) has Assassins gain thieves skills at 1st level (also the OSRIC method). If checked, will not start having thieves skills until 3rd level. In both cases an assassin at level 3 has thieves skills equivilent to level 1.
Default (Option A) is that Monk movement rate only applies at Normal encumbrance; afterwards  heavy is at 9', very heavy at 6', and encumbered is at 3'.
Option B (Implied OSRIC method), when this box is checked has Movement rate reduced by 1/4 for each encumbrance step past normal.
Option C, when this box is checked, has movement reduced by 3' for each encumbrance step with beyond 'enbumbered' going to 0 as normal.
Default is to use AD&D movement rates for short races (Dwarves, Gnomes & Halflings) of 9" maximum. If this box is checked will make the movement rate for short races the same as Humans, 12" maximum.

Default is to use AD&D 1e movement rates. With halflings, dwarves and Gnomes having a base movement of 9".
If this box is checked will use OSRIC encumbrance rates that decrements by 1/4 your normal movement rate for each encumbrance level. This will over-ride "Monk movement & encumbrance" choice above if chosen.
Default is to use AD&D 1e Non-Lethal and Weaponless Combat Procedures (DMG 72). if this box is checked OSRIC Unarmed Combat numbers will be shown instead (OSRIC PG 105).
PENDING (waiting for OSRIC 3e): This option uses OSRIC, numbers. Many were changed from 1e due to IP concerns (e.g. Fighter XP progression).
Magical Adjustment is AC adjustment from magical rings, robes etc.
Touch attacks use both dexterity modifier and benefits from magic bracers & rings
The +2 rear attack bonus is not accounted for in the AC calculations, so should be added as a +2 bonus to the attackers attack roll.

BTHB = “Base to Hit” Bonus. This is provided as an alternate for those that don't want to use the "To hit" roll matrix.

1. For Ascending AC add this number to your attack d20 roll + any magic (M) or situation (S, e.g. +2 for attacks from behind) bonuses to determine what AC you hit (d20+BTHB+M+S = AC that you hit)

2. For Descending AC (DAC) add this number to your attack d20 roll + any magic or situation bonuses and subtract oponents AC, if you score a 20 or above you hit (d20+BTHB+M+S-DAC ≥ 20 is a successful hit).

For both, if you roll a natural 20 on the d20, add an additional +5 to your roll.
Surprise has no negative modifiers to AC in the core books

Saving Throws do not include bonuses (those are autocalculated, AU8:AU17, Dwarves, Gnomes, and Halflings, but should be added to the die roll when rolling a save if it is magical in nature or poison). Saving Throws do include bonuses for Paladins (as these get added to all saves).
NOTE: per MM, Gnomes do get constitution bonus to Poison saves.
Halflings per MM pg 50, get a +3 attack bonus for slings and bows (not crossbows, or long bows though).
STR bonus for to-hit and damage apply to thrown weapons and they stack with DEX to-hit modifiers. (Source: Polyhedron, issue #2, Dispel Confusion column, "Official Answers to your AD&D questions")
Encumberance effect on Surprise segment bonus/penalty done per OSRIC

As noted in Polyhedron, A PC that is either a Druid, Paladin, or Monk may not take a 2nd class. Any other class that takes a 2nd class in either Druid, Paladin, or Monk, must forever abide by the restrictions of those classes (even when that class level is exceeded by the new one).

Dwarves, Gnomes and Halflings cannot use the longbow or any weapon over 12' in length. Gnomes and Halflings cannot use heavy crossbows, two handed swords, or pole arms over 200 gp in weight (DMG 102: Height & Weight of races. PHB 19: Characters under 5’ height cannot employ the longbow or any weapon over 12’ in length. Those under 100 pounds of body weight cannot use the heavy crossbow or pole arms in excess of 200 gold piece weight equivalent, including two-handed swords.

For thieves, the chance of casting failure from a scroll and chance of mishap per Polyhedron #25 and DMG 128. E.g. for failure purposes a 10th level thief = 1st level caster, and gains an additional caster level each level thereafter. Difficulty to cast is decrimented by 5% per level above thief casting level, per DMG rules on pg 128.
Assassins are the same, but gain the ability at 12th, rather than 10th level.

Base movement rate for Dwarves, Gnomes and Halflings is 9". This is "hidden/implied" in the Monster Manual entries for each. E.g. the Dwarf is listed as a movement rate of 6" and wearing chainmail (for a human chainmail is a movement rate of 9"). 6" movement applies to heavy and very heavy encumbrance.
